solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Jar filled with a colourful liquid (5)

indicatorNotes.filled with: a jar filled with something has that something inside it, so A goes into the jar

blocks.note: a jar is a pint of beer
kept as printed, placed inside PINT

annotation.surface: Someone describes a glass jar full of some brightly coloured drink.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'jar' is British slang for a glass of beer, usually a pint, so the jar here is a drink rather than a pot of paint.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: paint is the liquid whose whole purpose is to add colour.

entries.clue: Steal old currency tucked inside thin coat (8)

indicatorNotes.tucked inside: something tucked inside a coat is held within it, so the currency goes into the coat's letters

blocks.note: a thin layer of metal, as in silver plate
the European Currency Unit, forerunner of the euro

annotation.surface: A thief hides stolen old coins inside the lining of a thin coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The coat is not a garment but a coating: the surface wants a lining to hide cash in, but the thin coat is metal plating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in a formal register: peculating is embezzling, stealing money you were trusted with.

entries.clue: I hear about two notes in worship (8)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so I and TRY go round the two notes

blocks.note: kept as printed
DO and LA from the sol-fa scale
a judge hears, or tries, a case

annotation.surface: Someone says they hear a couple of notes sung during a church service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the courtroom sense, a judge hearing a case, not listening to music; the notes sit between I and TRY.
annotation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of idols, and the word is also used loosely for any excessive worship.

entries.clue: Queen hit, Don’t Stop Me Now (3,4,4,2,2)

blocks.note: a 1991 single by the rock band Queen
the plea of someone who insists on carrying on

annotation.surface: A reader names Queen's hit song Don't Stop Me Now.
annotation.walkthrough: Don't Stop Me Now is also a Queen hit, so the clue looks like it names one song; it is really a phrase meaning carry on regardless.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a Queen song title; the second is an idiom meaning keep going whatever happens.

entries.clue: Out, local female in hat (9)

indicatorNotes.in: a woman in a hat is inside it, so SHE goes inside LID

blocks.note: your local is your neighbourhood pub
lid is slang for a hat
a female, placed inside LID

annotation.surface: A woman from the area is out and about wearing a hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local' is a pub, the British word for the one nearest your home; 'Out' is the definition, not a stroll.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the book trade: a new title is out once it is on sale.

entries.clue: Lap up in game (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, reading up means reading LOOP from the bottom

blocks.note: a lap of a track is one loop

annotation.surface: An animal laps up its drink during a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lap up' looks like drinking; the lap is a circuit and 'up' turns it round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pool is one game played with cues on a table.

entries.clue: Villain’s broken rank to stop one going up and down (4,6)

annotation.definitionNote: Villain's reads as 'villain is', the answer is the noun

indicatorNotes.broken: RANK is broken up and rearranged
indicatorNotes.to stop: stopping a gap means plugging it, so the jumbled letters fill the inside of BOBBER

blocks.note: something that bobs, such as a fishing float
RANK rearranged, placed inside BOBBER after the B

annotation.surface: A villain's troops have broken ranks, trying to halt someone bobbing about.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Villain's' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; rank is not a line of soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a robber of banks is one kind of villain.

entries.clue: That legion slaughtered, number totally exposed (2,3,10)

indicatorNotes.slaughtered: the letters of THAT LEGION are cut to pieces and reassembled

blocks.note: THAT LEGION rearranged
something that numbs, an old anaesthetic

annotation.surface: A Roman legion is massacred, its whole number of men left defenceless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a count but a thing that numbs, so read it as numb-er. 'In the altogether' is British for naked.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be in the altogether is to be stark naked, with everything on show.

entries.clue: Wind or gas in thermal? (3,3)

blocks.note: empty, boastful talk
a thermal is a rising column of warm air

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether it is wind or some other gas in a rising thermal.
annotation.walkthrough: Both 'wind' and 'gas' also mean idle talk, which is the first sense. The question mark flags the literal second one.
annotation.definitionFit: Wind is empty talk, the first sense; the second is literal, since a thermal is warm air rising.

entries.clue: One refusing a measure of hose (6)

blocks.note: one who denies
the unit of fineness for stocking yarn

annotation.surface: Someone turns down a length of garden hose.
annotation.walkthrough: Hose here means stockings and tights, not a garden hose. The two senses are pronounced differently.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the agent noun from deny; the other is the unit that grades how sheer tights are.

entries.clue: Fold last of pages in dictionary inside comic (5,4)

indicatorNotes.last of: only the final letter of 'pages' is used
indicatorNotes.in: a letter in a dictionary is within it, so S is placed inside OED
indicatorNotes.inside: the dictionary sitting inside the comic means OSED is placed within CLOWN

blocks.note: a comic performer
the Oxford English Dictionary
final letter of pages, placed inside OED

annotation.surface: A comic folds the last few pages of a dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a container within a container. 'Fold' looks like creasing paper, which fits the pages, but it is a business failing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from business: a firm that folds stops trading.

entries.clue: Monster secure, it’s reported (5)

indicatorNotes.it’s reported: a report is something said aloud, so the answer is the spoken sound of the word for secure

blocks.note: to tighten is to make secure

annotation.surface: News comes in that a monster has been secured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secure' is a verb here, to make fast, not the adjective safe.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a titan is a giant, and monster also means something huge.

entries.clue: That man behind alto, when sozzled, can’t stand (6)

indicatorNotes.when sozzled: sozzled means drunk, and the drunk ALTO staggers into a new order
indicatorNotes.behind: HE comes after the jumbled ALTO

blocks.note: ALTO rearranged
a man, as a pronoun

annotation.surface: A man stands behind a drunken alto singer who can't stay on her feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can't stand' looks like a drunk falling over; it means dislike.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: not being able to stand someone means detesting them.

entries.clue: Recess measures one metre exactly at the opening, caver finally going in (4,4)

indicatorNotes.going in: a caver going in enters the space, so R enters FEET

blocks.note: units of length
last letter of caver, placed inside FEET after the F
the Roman numeral
the standard abbreviation
first letter of exactly

annotation.surface: A caver measures the mouth of a cave recess at exactly one metre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a nook in rock, which fits the caver, but it is a break from school or work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a recess is a break from work or lessons, time that is your own.

entries.clue: Alert operative (8,2)

blocks.note: sharp and aware
working, as a machine that is on

annotation.surface: An alert has gone out about a secret agent.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, an alarm and an agent; both are really adjectives.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a figurative idiom for a sharp mind; the second is literal, a device powered up and working.

entries.clue: 25 across, or what — does that suggest? (5,1,6)

blocks.note: OR WHAT rearranged
the missing word is the anagram indicator the solver must supply

annotation.surface: A cross-reference asks which missing word turns 'or what' into something mad.
annotation.walkthrough: Fill the dash with WOBBLY and 'or what wobbly' is itself an instruction: wobble OR WHAT. The answer describes its own wordplay, and 25 across is GO BANANAS.
annotation.definitionFit: Two British idioms for the same fit of temper: going bananas and throwing a wobbly.

entries.clue: Customs finally put foot down when character smuggled in object on domestic flight? (5,3)

indicatorNotes.smuggled in: smuggled goods are hidden inside something, so AIR is slipped inside TROD

blocks.note: last letter of Customs
stepped
an air is a manner or demeanour, placed inside TROD after the T

annotation.surface: A customs officer stamps down after a man smuggles contraband on an internal flight.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'domestic flight' is a flight of stairs in a house, not a plane. A stair rod holds the carpet into the back of each step.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: a flight is also a run of stairs, and a stair rod sits on each step of it.

entries.clue: King Charlie not prepared to carry key climbing gear (8)

indicatorNotes.to carry: to carry something is to hold it, so RAW holds the key inside it
indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down entry, climbing means reading RAEW upwards

blocks.note: chess abbreviation
a charlie is a fool, as is a nit
raw means unprepared, uncooked
a musical key, placed inside RAW after RA

annotation.surface: King Charles hasn't packed a key before going climbing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climbing gear' is not a unit: 'climbing' reverses the RAW-plus-E piece, leaving 'gear' as the definition. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: gear means clothes, and knitted jumpers and cardigans are one kind.

entries.clue: Humiliate further and give it some welly? (3,3,4,2)

blocks.note: to attack someone already down
literally, to kick hard

annotation.surface: Someone is urged to crush a beaten opponent and put real effort into it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give it some welly' is British for put your back into it; a welly is a wellington boot, hence the literal kick.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is the idiom for kicking someone when they are down; the second takes the welly, a boot, literally.

entries.clue: Diamonds get cooler (3,3)

blocks.note: slang for diamonds
to bag something is to get it

annotation.surface: Owning diamonds makes you cooler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like more fashionable, but it is a thing that cools.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a bag of ice is a device for cooling something.

entries.clue: Area for planting a bulb regularly lacking soil (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly lacking: every other letter of BULB is dropped, leaving UB

blocks.note: a flower bed
kept as printed
b U l B: the odd letters go

annotation.surface: A gardener plants a bulb in a bed that has no soil in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like garden earth, but it is the verb to dirty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in an old-fashioned register: to daub all over is to make dirty.

entries.clue: Fast runners, crooks did you say? (8)

indicatorNotes.did you say?: asking what someone said points to the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: crooks who cheat

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether the fast runners in a race are crooks.
annotation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CHEATERS and CHEETAHS sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: cheetahs are the fastest land animals.

entries.clue: Weather in Chartres is terrible (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: chartRES IS Terrible

annotation.surface: A tourist complains the weather in Chartres is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weather' is the verb, as in weather a storm.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to weather a storm is to hold out against it.

entries.clue: Olympian shows courage having lost lead (4)

blocks.note: DARES minus its first letter D

annotation.surface: An athlete at the Olympics shows grit despite losing the lead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' is not an athlete but a god of Mount Olympus; Ares is the Greek god of war.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Olympians were the gods of Mount Olympus, the war god among them.

entries.clue: Stand firmly against, do (5)

blocks.note: to cast a firm vote against, split into three short words
a do is a party

annotation.surface: An instruction to hold out firmly against doing something.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is split BE A NO. A beano is British for a party or celebration, and 'do' is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a whimsical split into BE A NO; the second is British slang, a beano being a knees-up.

entries.clue: Unknown chest found in Rhodes, unexpectedly (4,5)

indicatorNotes.found in: a thing found in a place is inside it, so ARK sits inside the jumbled RHODES
indicatorNotes.unexpectedly: RHODES turns up in an unforeseen order

blocks.note: RHODES rearranged, split D...HORSE
an ark is a chest, as in the Ark of the Covenant

annotation.surface: An unidentified chest is unexpectedly discovered on the Greek island of Rhodes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' reads as describing the chest, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from racing: a dark horse is a contender whose form nobody knows.

entries.clue: Blow a gasket while parked alongside West Indian housing block (2,7)

indicatorNotes.parked alongside: AS is set next to the rest
indicatorNotes.housing: housing something means giving it a home inside, so GOAN holds BAN within it

blocks.note: someone from Goa, on India's west coast
to bar, placed inside GOAN after GO
as meaning while

annotation.surface: Someone loses their temper while parked beside a Caribbean housing block.
annotation.walkthrough: 'West Indian' looks Caribbean; it is someone from western India. 'Housing block' is not a building but a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Two informal idioms for the same thing: blowing a gasket and going bananas both mean losing your temper.

entries.clue: Equestrian qualification (5)

blocks.note: one who sits on a horse
an added condition to a statement or contract

annotation.surface: A horse lover earns a riding certificate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Qualification' looks like a certificate, but it is a condition that qualifies an agreement.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is a person on horseback; the other is a clause added to qualify a document.
